short: A heavily armoured Soviet ground-attack aircraft that became the most produced combat aircraft in military history.
full:
The Ilyushin Il-2 Shturmovik was a Soviet ground-attack aircraft introduced in 1941, designed specifically to operate at low altitudes in support of advancing infantry and armour. Its defining feature was an integrated armour-steel tub that protected the engine, cockpit, and crucial fuel systems, earning it the nickname "the flying tank". This heavy protection allowed the aircraft to survive immense anti-aircraft fire and small-arms hits that would have destroyed conventional bombers.

Serving exclusively on the Eastern Front, the Il-2 became the primary aerial weapon of the Red Army against German mechanized forces, destroying thousands of tanks, trucks, and artillery pieces. Production reached staggering levels, with over thirty-six thousand built during the war, fulfilling Joseph Stalin's declaration that the aircraft was as essential to the Red Army as "air and bread". It remained a symbol of Soviet resilience and industrial might.
